stem_note: Shared stems ("For the following exercises, find dy/dx for the given functions", governing 175-184; the tangent-line-and-graph stem, governing 185-190; "find d^2y/dx^2 for the given functions", governing 191-196; "use the quotient rule to derive the given equations", governing 205-207; "find the requested higher-order derivative for the given functions", governing 209-213) are copied into each governed exercise as a self-contained instruction. Exercises 185-190 and 202's sketch-labeled parts (a), (c), (f) ask the student to graph or sketch a function from its own given formula, not to read a book-supplied figure, matching the precedent already used for the [T] graphing exercises in 3_1.json (#379, #386), 3_3.json (#118-121, #133-136), and 3_4.json (#171-173); classified symbolic/available accordingly. No exercise in this section reads a book-supplied graph, table, or figure.

exercises.text: Find dy/dx for y = x^2 - sec x + 1.
Find dy/dx for y = 3 csc x + 5/x.
Find dy/dx for y = x^2 cot x.
Find dy/dx for y = x - x^3 sin x.
Find dy/dx for y = sec x / x.
Find dy/dx for y = sin x tan x.
Find dy/dx for y = (x + cos x)(1 - sin x).
Find dy/dx for y = tan x / (1 - sec x).
Find dy/dx for y = (1 - cot x) / (1 + cot x).
Find dy/dx for y = cos x (1 + csc x).
[T] Find an equation of the tangent line to f(x) = -sin x at x = 0. Then use a calculator to graph both the function and the tangent line to ensure the equation for the tangent line is correct.
[T] Find an equation of the tangent line to f(x) = csc x at x = pi/2. Then use a calculator to graph both the function and the tangent line to ensure the equation for the tangent line is correct.

[T] Find an equation of the tangent line to f(x) = 1 + cos x at x = 3pi/2. Then use a calculator to graph both the function and the tangent line to ensure the equation for the tangent line is correct.
[T] Find an equation of the tangent line to f(x) = sec x at x = pi/4. Then use a calculator to graph both the function and the tangent line to ensure the equation for the tangent line is correct.
[T] Find an equation of the tangent line to f(x) = x^2 - tan x at x = 0. Then use a calculator to graph both the function and the tangent line to ensure the equation for the tangent line is correct.
[T] Find an equation of the tangent line to f(x) = 5 cot x at x = pi/4. Then use a calculator to graph both the function and the tangent line to ensure the equation for the tangent line is correct.
Find d^2y/dx^2 for y = x sin x - cos x.
Find d^2y/dx^2 for y = sin x cos x.
Find d^2y/dx^2 for y = x - (1/2) sin x.
Find d^2y/dx^2 for y = 1/x + tan x.
Find d^2y/dx^2 for y = 2 csc x.
Find d^2y/dx^2 for y = sec^2 x.
Find all x values on the graph of f(x) = -3 sin x cos x where the tangent line is horizontal.
Find all x values on the graph of f(x) = x - 2 cos x for 0 < x < 2pi where the tangent line has slope 2.
Let f(x) = cot x. Determine the points on the graph of f for 0 < x < 2pi where the tangent line(s) is (are) parallel to the line y = -2x.

[T] A mass on a spring bounces up and down in simple harmonic motion, modeled by the function s(t) = -6 cos t where s is measured in inches and t is measured in seconds. Find the rate at which the spring is oscillating at t = 5 s.

Let the position of a swinging pendulum in simple harmonic motion be given by s(t) = a cos t + b sin t where a and b are constants, t measures time in seconds, and s measures position in centimeters. If the position is 0 cm and the velocity is 3 cm/s when t = 0, find the values of a and b.

After a diver jumps off a diving board, the edge of the board oscillates with position given by s(t) = -5 cos t cm at t seconds after the jump. (a) Sketch one period of the position function for t >= 0. (b) Find the velocity function. (c) Sketch one period of the velocity function for t >= 0. (d) Determine the times when the velocity is 0 over one period. (e) Find the acceleration function. (f) Sketch one period of the acceleration function for t >= 0.

The number of hamburgers sold at a fast-food restaurant in Pasadena, California, is given by y = 10 + 5 sin x where y is the number of hamburgers sold and x represents the number of hours after the restaurant opened at 11 a.m. until 11 p.m., when the store closes. Find y' and determine the intervals where the number of burgers being sold is increasing.

[T] The amount of rainfall per month in Phoenix, Arizona, can be approximated by y(t) = 0.5 + 0.3 cos t, where t is months since January. Find y' and use a calculator to determine the intervals where the amount of rain falling is decreasing.
Use the quotient rule to derive the following equation: d/dx(cot x) = -csc^2 x.
Use the quotient rule to derive the following equation: d/dx(sec x) = sec x tan x.
Use the quotient rule to derive the following equation: d/dx(csc x) = -csc x cot x.
Use the definition of derivative and the identity cos(x + h) = cos x cos h - sin x sin h to prove that d(cos x)/dx = -sin x.
Find d^3y/dx^3 for y = 3 cos x.
Find d^2y/dx^2 for y = 3 sin x + x^2 cos x.
Find d^4y/dx^4 for y = 5 cos x.
Find d^2y/dx^2 for y = sec x + cot x.
Find d^3y/dx^3 for y = x^10 - sec x.
